suggested_services_note: Each row is one way this kind of work takes money (one of the master's 28 paths per flow). The owner keeps the services that fit and picks ONE path per service and place. Names and amounts are examples from the profession file, not prices.

suggested_services.name: Intro call
suggested_services.example: The main story: a free 30-minute intro call by phone with Maya. Nothing is taken, a YES books it, and nothing is paid through Rosie. If Alex becomes a client later, the firm's fees are billed in its own tools or from Alex's accounts.

suggested_services.name: Home meeting
suggested_services.example: The main story: a free 60-minute meeting about retiring, at Alex's home, with Marcus. Nothing is taken, and Rosie sends no bill. Any plan or advisory fees are the firm's own, outside Rosie.

before_times: What would you like help with? Retirement, investments, a plan, or something else.
Which state do you live in? The state only.
By phone, by video or at the office? Or at your home?
An adviser by name, or the soonest one? Rosie never ranks or suggests one.
after_time: Are you still working? Yes or no.
Will a spouse or partner join? Yes or no.
How did you hear about the adviser? A few words, like 'a coworker'.
Anything that helps the call, like an interpreter, a larger font or a step-free way in.
secure_page_only: Is it safe to text you? If not, how should the business reach you?
A home meeting: the street address, kept only as where to meet
A switch, on by default: the firm's required disclosures, like its client relationship summary, to read before the first meeting
A switch, on by default: a trusted contact, if the client wants to name one (name and phone), whom the firm may call if it can't reach the client or is worried about them. Optional, never pressed
A tick: Rosie books the adviser's time only. It isn't an adviser and gives no investment, tax or legal advice
A tick: texts are about this booking only
intake_questions.never_asked: Account numbers, balances, savings amounts, income, Social Security numbers, tax ID or bank numbers, health details, or statements. The firm gathers what it needs in its own tools after the call. Never anything about race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (beyond 18 or older) or disability.
intake_questions.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. A spouse or partner may be added on the secure page. Another adult, like a grown child, may book for a parent, but the parent gives their own yes on the secure page and takes the call.

stop: someone is in danger right now
go_on: someone pushing the customer to send money, buy gift cards or crypto, or move savings right now
a stranger or a new online friend asking for account details or money
a family member or caregiver pressing an older client about their money

what_rosie_says.pushed to send or move money: This sounds like a scam. Please don't send money or share account details. The national Elder Fraud Hotline helps people 60 and older: 833-372-8311. Anyone can report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. The booking goes on.
what_rosie_says.pressed by family or a caregiver: The adviser talks with the client alone first. The booking goes on, and Sam is told, with no family details in the text.

prep: Have a short list of questions. No statements or account numbers are needed for this call, and please never text any.
required: None. The free intro call is the first step. The client agreement, disclosures and account details come after it, in the firm's own tools.

staff.skills: Retirement planning, investments, Social Security questions, workshops, Spanish.
staff.licenses_or_certificates: Each adviser: their own registration for each state they take clients in. Rosie shows it as given and doesn't check it.
staff.supervision: The firm's own supervision of its advisers stays in its own tools. An unregistered assistant, like Pat, only schedules.
staff.who_oks: Sam OKs office and home meetings. Sam may let each adviser OK their own.

children_and_age.who_may_book: An adult books for themselves. A spouse or partner may be added on the secure page. Another adult, like a grown child, may book for a parent, but the parent gives their own yes on the secure page and takes the call.

visit.check_in: Phone or video: the adviser asks for the 4-digit code at the start, which also shows they're talking to the person who booked. At the office: the code at the front desk. At a home: the code at the door.
visit.changes_at_visit: Extra time on the same call is free, with the customer's yes. A second call is its own booking.

license.note: Optional. Upload anything. Rosie never checks it and never shows it as checked (D96).
license.need: Always. Each adviser who gives advice: their own registration as an investment adviser representative where the client's state requires it. The firm: its own registration as an investment adviser, with the national regulator or the state, as its size and the state's rules say.
license.ask: Each adviser's CRD number, at sign-up or in their invite reply. The firm's CRD number, and the states it may advise clients in.
license.insurance: Default: none asked. A bond where the state's rules require it, from the state's form.
license.background: Part of the registration itself. Rosie adds none.

never_in_a_text: account numbers, balances, savings amounts or income
Social Security, tax ID or bank numbers
statements or documents of any kind
advice: what to buy, sell or hold, or what to expect to earn

pf.visit: the client lives in another state
